## Context
Recent GitHub Actions runs have remained stuck until another session manually cleared them. Diagnose the recurring cause using authenticated GitHub evidence without mutating workflow or run state.

## Plan
- Inspect recent Actions runs, jobs, queue/concurrency metadata, cancellation history, and workflow definitions.
- Correlate the stuck runs with triggering events, reusable-workflow structure, runner labels, concurrency groups, and repository limits.
- Distinguish the immediate clearing action from the systemic root cause and record evidence-backed remediation options.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The affected run or run pattern is identified with URLs and timestamps, checked via `gh run list` and Actions API run metadata.
- [ ] The mechanism that leaves runs stuck is explained from Actions API job metadata and `.github/workflows/` evidence.
- [ ] Competing hypotheses are checked against repository concurrency settings, runner labels, and recent run history.
- [ ] Findings and a focused remediation recommendation are recorded in a `rebar comment` on this ticket.

## Verification
Use read-only `gh run list`, `gh run view`, and `gh api` queries, plus inspection of `.github/workflows/`. Cross-check run-level status against job-level timestamps and conclusions. No run cancellation, rerun, dispatch, workflow edit, or repository-setting change is authorized.

## File impact
Read-only diagnosis; no repository files will be modified.
